title: Manthara's whisper
hookLine: how a whisper works: not one big lie, but a picture of the future, told over and over
carry: satsang: the company you keep shapes the mind
last: I SEE NO DIFFERENCE BETWEEN THEM.

cards: Someone takes you aside. They're not angry at you; they're worried for you. Haven't you noticed, they say, how things are going to go?
And they paint you a picture of next year, and in it you're smaller, and someone else is laughing. Nothing they've said is quite a lie. But by the end, people you loved an hour ago look different.
That's what happens in Kaikeyi's room tonight, and it's why Hindu teachers care so much about whose voice you sit with.

teach.b: Manthara throws away the jewel and starts building the picture. Once Rama is king, she says, his son will be king after him, and Bharata will be cut out of the line forever.

Worse, a king fears his brothers: Rama will send Bharata away, or have him killed. And you, she tells Kaikeyi, were the king's favorite. Now Kausalya will be queen mother, and you'll stand in her hall like a servant.
Kaikeyi pushes back at first. Rama is the eldest, she says. He's good, he's truthful, he treats me like his own mother.
She doesn't fall at the first push. But Manthara keeps going, the picture gets sharper, and slowly Kaikeyi's face changes.
By the end she's asking: how do we stop this? Why did Manthara do it? Valmiki gives her loyalty to Kaikeyi and Bharata, and plenty of bitterness.
Later retellings, like Tulsidas's Ramcharitmanas, add that the gods asked the goddess Sarasvati to turn her mind, so Rama would go to the forest and, in time, defeat Ravana.
Either way, many Hindu teachers read this scene as a lesson about company. The word is sanga.
Satsang is the company of the true and the good; kusang is bad company.

teach.h: THE MIND TAKES THE COLOR OF ITS COMPANY.
teach.b: It's part of why families gather to sing bhajans together, why a grandmother wants you at the temple: the mind takes the color of what it keeps hearing.
Kaikeyi, who had equal eyes an hour ago, turned in one night with the wrong voice in her ear.

how: In Ramlila and in homes where the Ramcharitmanas is read, the goddess Sarasvati turns Manthara's mind at the gods' request; readers of Valmiki often note that his telling leaves the motive human.

o: the queen mother who rules while Rama is crowned
a nurse who warns Kausalya about the coronation
the maid who turns Kaikeyi's joy into fear

p: paints a future where Bharata is lost
would be queen mother, Manthara warns
turns Manthara's mind in later retellings

s: Kaikeyi gives in at the first word
she defends Rama at first: he's the eldest, and treats her as his mother.
Valmiki says a goddess made Manthara speak
that comes in later retellings like Tulsidas's; Valmiki keeps the motive human.
Manthara warns that Bharata could be sent away or killed
that's the heart of the picture she paints.

games.q: you're Kaikeyi. your oldest companion says Rama's crowning will ruin your son. what do you say first?
o: Rama is the eldest and good; Bharata may reign after him.
you're right; tell me what to do.
games.why: Kaikeyi defends Rama first. only as Manthara keeps going does her face change, until she asks how to stop it.

practice: Think of a picture of the future someone handed you lately, about you or about another person, and notice whose voice it's in. Then put a better voice beside it.
If you pray, let it be a name, a bhajan you know, or a line your grandparents say, and let that voice speak last. If you don't pray, let it be the voice of the wisest person you know.

wordCard.voice: Manthara. The maid who turns Kaikeyi's joy into fear, not with one big lie but with a picture of a future in which Bharata is lost, told until it sticks.

orig.note: Sanskrit sat-saṅga: company with the true or the good. its opposite, ku-saṅga, is bad company.

carryVoice: Your line: satsang, the company you keep shapes the mind. A picture of the future isn't the future yet. Day five hundred eighteen, and the week is done.
